sourceInformation.source: Kaboom! (Activision, Atari 2600, 1981), designed by Larry Kaplan
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGL 2 fallback; Rapier 3D compat 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; PeerJS 1.5.5; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0; esbuild 0.25.12
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded geometry, dark ink outlines, mint and coral rooftop district, paper grain and comic typography
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and NumberKeyframeTrack for idle, throwing, laughing and bucket recoil; procedural particles and trails
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated music, splash and explosion effects, and formant-filtered gibberish voices; music defaults to 10 percent; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub host-authoritative shared-world co-op for 1–4 players; standalone room-code WebRTC co-op through PeerJS signaling, with BroadcastChannel for same-browser rooms; local 1–2 player co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium: standalone software WebGPU state checks, WebGL visual inspection at 1920×1080 and phone size, deterministic simulation and full 172-bomb/eight-round playthrough, emulated standard gamepad, touch, offline audio rendering, local co-op, isolated-context WebRTC using a local PeerServer, and official AI Hub harness in headless Three.js scene mode for two/four players, latency/jitter/loss, host departure and dedicated server. Physical controller, human listening, real mobile hardware and WAN/public relay availability: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Read Activision's original Kaboom! manual and scoring table via Atari Compendium and AtariAge; consulted archived gameplay screenshots and sound descriptions; read AI Hub's protocol, client and harness, Three.js r180 source, and PeerJS official documentation. Sources: https://www.ataricompendium.com/archives/manuals/vcs/kaboom.pdf ; https://atariage.com/manual_html_page.php?SoftwareLabelID=257 ; https://www.atariage.com/screenshot_page.php?SoftwareLabelID=257 ; https://www.honestgamers.com/1362/atari-2600/kaboom/review.html ; https://github.com/michaelcrosato/ai-hub/tree/main/lib/hub ; https://peerjs.com/client/getting-started
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux, Ubuntu 26.04 on WSL2

testingFeedback: 10 tracked issue groups were caught across game presentation, input, renderer compatibility and test setup; repeated failing checks are grouped by root cause in development-issues.json. Final verification: 112 of 112 checks passed.

2 were game blocking in headless session testing: renderer initialization stalls and a network loop coupled to frame visibility. Rendering-free protocol tests isolate the remaining software rasterization timing limits; rendering performance is outside scope.

The official four-player AI Hub harness with latency, jitter and packet loss exposed lifecycle and networking problems that solo play did not reveal. The deterministic full shift also verified all 172 bombs are catchable.
WebGPU screenshots were least helpful because this headless software adapter can produce a blank canvas. WebGL screenshots were used for visual inspection instead.
engineFeedback: Three.js's native toon materials, orthographic camera and animation mixer made a cohesive illustrated stage possible with procedural geometry.

Software WebGPU initialization and asynchronous shader compilation were unreliable across multiple frames. I added software-adapter fallback, startup recovery and a headless Three.js scene mode for protocol tests.
The arcade rules, controller-first menus, procedural audio and authoritative multiplayer state synchronization.
Coordinating asynchronous rendering, physics, controller input and network lifecycle without making shared-world simulation depend on frame visibility.
none; compatibility handling and the headless scene path are application code, with the engine and AI Hub client unmodified.
Provide a small first-party controller UI and deterministic game-loop toolkit alongside the renderer.
promptFeedback: The source, presentation requirements and explicit completion criteria gave the game a clear creative direction.
The source's eight endless difficulty groups needed an interpretation for a finite, complete demo; this game uses eight rounds and optional overtime.
Combining a standalone single-file game, controller and touch UX, and both standalone and AI Hub multiplayer into one polished slice.
Specify whether standalone online play should depend on a public signaling service or require manual peer exchange.

aiHub.name: Kaboomerang
aiHub.tagline: A little splash. A lot of nerve.
aiHub.description: A mischievous rooftop bomber. Three buckets of nerve. Catch twisting bomb patterns, build a streak and unleash splashback through eight escalating rounds, solo or with your bucket brigade.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick, D-pad, A/D, arrows, mouse or touch drag. Splashback: Cross/A, Space or tap. Pause: Options/Escape. Local P2: J/L and I, or a second controller.
